text:
Devin (AE): quick one — customer is asking for recommended topology for their Azure POC. they have an existing Virtual Hub + onprem SD-WAN. want low-latency + ability to preserve client IP for rate-limiting. do we advise Virtual Hub VNet peering or PrivateLink/Private Endpoint behind ExpressRoute?

Sophie (SE): @Devin good q. short answer: depends on trust boundary and whether customer needs hub-centric routing. if they want hub controls (FW, inspection) + BGP over ExpressRoute, use ExpressRoute/Virtual Hub. if they want direct secure control plane to our Private endpoint and simpler firewall rules, PrivateLink is cleaner.

Liam (NetOps): adding network ops view — preserve client IP across privatelink is tricky; we typically see source IP NAT at the connector unless customers use a NAT/forwarding appliance in front. with ExpressRoute + transit, you can preserve source if they NAT appropriately.

Erin (Sales Eng): pricing note: ExpressRoute egress bandwidth cost + Azure circuit fees vs PrivateLink data processing and endpoint charges. customer asked for 95th percentile estimate. can we give a rough delta?

Sophie (SE): rough guidance: for sustained high bandwidth (multi-Gbps) ExpressRoute is often cheaper. for bursty low-volume traffic, PrivateLink + paid per-GB can be simpler. i'll ping infra for sample numbers.

Liam (NetOps): firewall rules snippet they can hand to netsec:
```
allow outbound TCP 443 to 52.23.11.0/24 (redwood-privatelink)
allow outbound TCP 443 to 40.79.200.0/22 (redwood-azure-egress)
allow inbound TCP 32768-61000 for tcp-client-keepalive (if using NAT traversal)
```
note: concrete IP blocks will vary by region — customer must fetch our published egress range.

Devin (AE): customer also has security questionnaire asking about mTLS and TLS inspect. they want to know if we terminate TLS at our endpoint or if mutual TLS to our service is possible.

Sophie (SE): we support mutual TLS for Private/PrivateLink connections. for ExpressRoute with a gateway and proxy in their VNet, they can TLS-terminate in their infra or forward encrypted. if they need TLS inspect we recommend a hub firewall that does TLS-inspect before traffic reaches our connector.

Erin (Sales Eng): operational ask: we need to hand off to their network team for a connectivity test. can NetOps provide a minimal runbook + test commands?

Liam (NetOps): yes — minimal connectivity test: 
1) customer pings our test IP (we'll provide)
2) curl https://health-check.redwood-inference.internal/ -v and capture TLS handshake
3) traceroute to our endpoint from their egress
we'll provide a small JSON sample for SNI header checks if they use TLS-inspect.

NetOpsBot: automated note — please ensure customer adds our egress CIDRs to allowlist before scheduled test. see https://status.redwood.ai/egress-cidrs

Devin (AE): timeline — customer wants POC in 2 weeks. can we commit to providing IPs, runbook, and rough cost delta by EOD tomorrow?

Sophie (SE): i can draft the runbook today and include a short matrix: pros/cons (latency, preserve-srcip, cost, inspection). will attach to thread once ready.

Liam (NetOps): i'll pull region-specific egress ranges and a sample iptables/snort rule for their security team. owner: @Liam.

Erin (Sales Eng): i'll book a 30-min handoff call with customer net team for Tue 10am PT. Devin — i'll add you + Sophie + Liam.

Devin (AE): perfect. last ask from customer: do we support automatic fallback from PrivateLink to ExpressRoute if endpoint capacity hits limits?

Sophie (SE): not out-of-the-box. we can design a dual-path with healthchecks and a custom routing policy (requires customer routing controls and our routing config). that's an engineering effort but doable for enterprise customers. i'll raise a small RFC if they need it.

Liam (NetOps): action items: 
- Liam: publish egress ranges + firewall snippet (TODAY)
- Sophie: runbook + decision matrix (TODAY)
- Erin: schedule handoff call (ASAP)
- Devin: confirm customer's forecasted bandwidth and whether they will deploy a hub FW (BYEOD?)

Devin (AE): thanks team — sending customer an ack and will add bandwidth numbers.

NetOpsBot: reminder: attach the SOC2/network-architecture packet if requested by customer security questionnaire.

Sophie (SE): noted — i'll include the packet in the runbook.

Erin (Sales Eng): thanks all :thumbsup:

Devin (AE): closing loop — i'll post customer confirmation in this thread after the call.
